jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Sodali & Co is a recognized global capital markets stakeholder advisory firm, serving over 2,000 clients in more than 65 countries. The Firm advises a diverse and global client base including many of the world’s largest companies. Formed by the mergers of several market-leading capital markets stakeholder engagement consultancies, Sodali is the largest global shareholder services firm in the world. The Firm operates out of three global headquarters in New York, London, and Sydney and is supported by 12 regional offices in major financial capitals around the world.

Sodali provides a full suite of shareholder, sustainability, and strategic communications advisory services that, together, enable the Firm to deliver clients differentiated insights, integrated expertise, and bespoke advice to address complex interconnected issues, identify and capitalize on strategic opportunities, and drive successful business outcomes.

Sodali’s Services Include

Shareholder Advisory services include M&A Advisory, Activism Preparation and Defense, Board Governance Services, Corporate Governance Advisory, Proxy Solicitation, Capital Markets Intelligence, Global Debt and Bondholder Services, and Stakeholder Research.
Sustainability services include ESG Assessment, Strategy & Implementation, and Communications Advisory.
Strategic Communications services include Corporate Communications, Financial and Transaction Communications, Investor Relations, Public Affairs and Campaigns, Crisis and Special Situations, and Research.

The Opportunity

The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) will be a strategic leader in Sodali’s growth strategy. This individual will work with the Global Heads of our core practices, Finance, People, Business Operations, and Data Analytics to unite our technology strategy and our core business lines to drive real impact in our approach to data security, infrastructure, innovation, and data commercialization, and align technology initiatives with our business priorities. In this position, the CTO will be involved in matters related to agentic security, Snowflake administration, Azure deployment, cloud services, RFP management and ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2 audits. This role will lead the IT help desk team and office infrastructure teams globally.

This position is located in New York. Relocation assistance is not available for this position.

Key Responsibilities

Implement best-in-class IT operations and infrastructure across the firm globally. This includes updating systems, cybersecurity, and setting global IT policies.
Lead digital transformation, update infrastructure, strengthen cybersecurity, and enabling scalable systems that support Sodali’s worldwide footprint
Drive security governance standards, including remaining aware of any regional shifts in compliance or security standards.
Lead global IT improvement projects while adhering to regional compliance requirements.
Improve resiliency and efficiency of current systems and infrastructure.
Deploy Azure and cloud services with an eye for streamlining processes and procedures
Coordinate with internal stakeholders regarding .
Align technology strategy with overall business priorities, including staying agile as priorities expand with a high-growth organization.
Champion innovation and emerging technology adoption — including AI and agentic systems — to create competitive advantage for the Firm.
Partner with Data Analytics and practice leaders to identify and develop opportunities to commercialize Sodali’s proprietary data assets.

Qualifications

12+ years of information technology experience, preferably in a high-growth, finance or professional-services environment.
Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, or a related field. Relevant certifications such as CISSP, PMP, or ITIL are preferred.
Strong experience managing a Microsoft environment.
Salesforce, NetSuite, and Snowflake Administration experience.
Experience managing GPU infrastructure for LLM training and inference preferred.
Proven success in developing and executing global, integrated strategies.
Experience driving innovation programs and identifying data monetization or commercialization opportunities preferred.
Experience managing integrations of mergers and acquisitions.
Strong experience partnering with advisory and executive leadership teams.
Track record of leading organizations through change, transformation, or scale.
Strategic and creative, with a strong focus on execution.
Exceptional communication and presentation skills; credible and influential at the executive level.
Comfort working in fast-paced, evolving environments where priorities may shift.
Proactive, self-starter, comfortable working in a flat organization.
Willingness to travel domestically and internationally as required.

Sodali & Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunities Employer.
We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment where everyone feels valued and respected. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals regardless of race, color, religion, sex (including sexual orientation, gender identity, and pregnancy), national origin, age, disability, or veteran status. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to support candidates with disabilities or access needs throughout the recruitment process.

jobs.title: Fractional Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
Rare is a global leader in community-led conservation. For more than 50 years, we have partnered with local communities worldwide to strengthen their stewardship of the lands and waters they depend on.

Today, Rare works in some of the world’s most biodiverse places, where climate risks are high and community-led conservation can deliver the greatest impact. We combine community-driven solutions with behavioral science, partnerships, financing, and practical innovation to create the conditions for conservation to succeed. By helping make local leadership the foundation of conservation, we strengthen resilience for people and nature.

As Rare seeks to scale these critically needed and effective conservation solutions, the organization is committed to modernizing our use of technology scale. The Fractional CIO will lead Rare’s transition from fragmented, locally managed systems to an integrated technology and operating environment built for intelligence at scale. This work will modernize the systems that underpin Rare’s work delivering impact to hundreds of thousands of people in dozens of countries. To achieve this transition, the role will concentrate on implementing Rare’s FY27 priorities:

Building and rolling out Salesforce for grants management
Selecting and implementing a global HRIS
Providing strategic guidance for Rare’s org-wide Microsoft 365 rollout, already underway
Guiding Rare’s Automation and Applied AI strategy

We are looking for a senior technology leader to drive key systems efforts while putting in place the governance and internal capacities needed for the long term. This is a delivery role, not an advisory one. You will own outcomes, manage implementation partners, and make architecture and investment decisions.

Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Strategy and Organizational Development, you will be supported by a cross-functional team with clear, complementary roles:

Rare’s Vice President of Technology:
and Rare’s Technology team will serve as the primary technical partner and will ensure alignment with Rare’s broader technology environment.
The Vice President of Learning and Development:
will lead change management and staff adoption.
The Director of Systems and Special Projects:
will bring knowledge of Rare’s systems and drive project management.
Leaders from Finance, Talent, Development, and Programs:
will guide process decisions and champion adoption within their teams. External implementation partners will bring specialized expertise and additional delivery capacity.
External implementation partners for Salesforce and a HRIS will bring specialized expertise and additional delivery capacity.

Expected Outcomes of the Engagement

Salesforce grants management designed, built, and rolling out.
Establish a consistent, transparent process from funding opportunity through grant closeout, delivered in phases in partnership with Development, Finance, and Programs. You will select and manage the implementation partner, ensuring high-quality delivery and value for money.
A global HRIS selected, contracted, and moving into implementation.
Lead requirements gathering, vendor selection, contracting, and implementation planning in partnership with Talent and other business owners, leaving Rare with a well-governed program underway.
Microsoft 365 strategically guided, not directly led.
The rollout is already underway and will remain with the internal project team. Your role will be to provide strategic guidance on governance, integration, and alignment with Rare’s broader technology architecture.

To support the implementation of these systems and sustain them over time, you will:

Establish clear decision rights and named owners for core platforms, data, integrations, security, vendors, and technology investments.
Define a coherent technology architecture, including standards for access, privacy, security, and business continuity, as well as authoritative sources for priority organizational data.
Recommend a technology operating model that identifies the leadership, staffing, capabilities, and external support Rare will need after the fractional engagement concludes.
Develop a short, prioritized set of automation and AI opportunities, with clear recommendations about where Rare should invest, scale, adapt, or stop.

Primary Responsibilities

Deliver Priority Systems

Lead Salesforce grants management design, implementation, and phased rollout, including selecting and managing the implementation partner ,
in partnership with Development, Finance, and Programs.
Guide HRIS requirements, vendor selection, contracting, implementation planning, and initial rollout in partnership with Talent and other business owners.
Hire and oversee implementation consultants for Salesforce and HRIS, ensuring delivery quality and value for money.
Provide light strategic guidance to the internal team leading Microsoft 365 migration and adoption.
Work with business owners to simplify and standardize priority processes before configuring technology around them.

Establish Governance and Integration

Develop and maintain technology governance practices in partnership with the Vice President of Technology, ensuring governance decisions are grounded in Rare’s existing environment.
Define platform ownership, product ownership, decision rights, data stewardship, and accountability across enterprise, regional, and country levels.
Establish lightweight governance for architecture, integrations, data, security, privacy, access, vendors, and technology investments.
Define how core platforms connect and which systems serve as authoritative sources for priority organizational data.
Incorporate cybersecurity, compliance, business continuity, and risk management into system and vendor decisions.

Enable Adoption and Internal Ownership

Partner with the Vice President of Learning and Development, who will lead change management, to ensure communication, staff engagement, and role-based support are built into each implementation.
Work closely with the Vice President of Technology and Technology team to align new platforms with Rare’s existing infrastructure, security, and support model.
Recommend a sustainable technology operating model and identify internal technology skills needed for Rare following the fractional engagement.

Guide Automation and Applied AI

Identify a small number of practical opportunities for automation and AI to improve staff effectiveness, organizational decision-making, or program delivery.
Align AI investments with Rare’s technology architecture, information governance, security, and change management approach.

Future Priorities

After gaining traction on the delivery of the FY27 priorities, assess Rare’s current technology strategy and present recommendations for the next phase of strategic priorities, investments, and implementation.

Experience and Qualifications

Over 10 years of senior technology leadership experience as a CIO, CTO, technology transformation leader, or equivalent advisor.
Demonstrated success leading enterprise systems modernization from strategy and architecture through implementation, adoption, and benefits realization.
Experience with Salesforce-based business platforms and HRIS selection and implementation.
Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 and SharePoint, system integration, enterprise data governance, cybersecurity, privacy, identity and access management, vendor management, and technology risk.
Experience coordinating internal teams, business owners, consultants, and vendors across multiple initiatives.
Experience working in a globally distributed or federated organization; nonprofit, international development, or conservation experience is helpful but not required.
Practical understanding of responsible AI and automation, including how to assess potential value, risks, and organizational readiness.

Leadership Approach

The successful candidate will be:
Strategic and hands-on, able to move between executive decisions and implementation detail.
Enterprise-minded while grounded in the needs of staff, programs, regions, and country teams.
Decisive and pragmatic, with the judgment to simplify, sequence, and stop work when evidence warrants it.
Effective at delivering results through cross-functional teams rather than relying on direct authority.
Committed to responsible, secure, inclusive, and sustainable uses of technology.
Impact oriented with a passion for Rare’s mission and the people we serve.

Time Commitment

The role will be 15-20 hours per week over the course of 11 months: November 2026 through September 2027.

How to Respond

Interested candidates should submit a résumé and a brief letter of interest (no more than one page) outlining:
Relevant experience leading comparable systems modernization efforts, particularly Salesforce and HRIS implementations, with examples of engagements and results achieved.
Availability from November 2026 through September 2027, including the ability to commit approximately 15–20 hours per week.
Proposed fees on an hourly, monthly, or engagement basis.

Please also provide names and contact information for two professional references.

Candidates responding on behalf of a firm should identify the individual who would serve as Fractional CIO and describe the roles of any additional team members.

Please send application materials to Renee Baiorunos at rbaiorunos@rare.org by October 23, 2026
. Selected candidates will be invited to discuss their experience, proposed approach, and fit with Rare’s cross-functional team.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, Cybersecurity Advisory Services
jobs.description:
Presidio, Where Teamwork and Innovation Shape the Future

At Presidio, we're at the forefront of a global technology revolution, transforming industries through cutting-edge digital solutions and next-generation AI. We empower businesses - and their internal customers - to achieve more through innovation, automation, and intelligent insights.

The Role

As a Senior Cybersecurity Consulting Leader with Presidio, you will be responsible for scaling an established Cyber Consulting Services organization and growing the business faster than market pace. You will lead Information Security Governance, Cybersecurity Architecture, and Offensive Security while owning the operating performance of the consulting portfolio. You will be accountable for revenue growth, gross profit and margin, utilization, delivery quality, backlog, capacity, and workforce strategy. You will lead through managers and principal consultants while maintaining technical and client credibility to challenge how the practice delivers, scales, and evolves.

Travel Requirements

This is a client-facing role. You will be required to travel up to 30% to client locations to deliver professional services when needed.

Responsibilities Include

Lead a distributed Cyber Consulting Services organization spanning Information Security Governance, Cybersecurity Architecture, and Offensive Security.
Grow the business faster than the cybersecurity services market while maintaining expectations for gross profit, gross margin, utilization, delivery quality, and client outcomes.
Own operating performance across revenue, GP/GM, utilization, backlog, capacity, project economics, delivery forecasting, and engagement health.
Build workforce plans that balance FTE capacity, skills, backlog, utilization, projected demand, and consulting economics.
Increase internally delivered services revenue by building FTE capability and using subcontractors selectively for specialized skills or capacity requirements.
Own subcontractor and third-party delivery strategy, including partner selection, economics, quality, capacity, performance, and appropriate use.
Lead, develop, and hold accountable managers responsible for consulting teams and individual contributors across multiple cybersecurity disciplines.
Own succession planning, leadership development, performance management, hiring strategy, career development, and retention across the consulting organization.
Establish operating mechanisms for resource forecasting, engagement governance, project reviews, quality control, utilization management, and delivery escalations.
Maintain executive oversight of major consulting engagements and intervene when delivery quality, project economics, client satisfaction, or contractual commitments are at risk.
Create, evolve, and retire consulting services based on client demand, delivery performance, market changes, technical developments, and the ability to scale delivery.
Define and improve consulting methodologies, delivery standards, costing models, level-of-effort models, and repeatable engagement structures.
Challenge Principal-level consultants and practice leaders on technical direction, methodology, service relevance, delivery quality, and opportunities to develop new capabilities.
Partner with Client Success Management, Sales, and pre-sales teams on strategic engagements, capacity requirements, client needs, and technical sales enablement.
Develop technical enablement that helps Sales and pre-sales teams identify, position, and qualify appropriate cybersecurity consulting opportunities.
Engage CISOs, CIOs, CTOs, and other executives during strategic engagements, client escalations, executive briefings, and consulting sponsorship activities.
Build collaboration across governance, architecture, and offensive security teams so clients can access integrated consulting capabilities rather than isolated technical services.

Required Skills And Professional Experience

Bachelor’s degree or the equivalent work experience and/or military experience
Minimum of 12-15 years of cybersecurity experience with progressively increasing leadership responsibility.
Significant leadership experience in cybersecurity consulting, advisory, professional services, or a comparable client-facing security organization.
Demonstrated experience leading managers as well as senior individual contributors, with experience operating geographically distributed teams of more than 20 people.
Experience leading a multi-disciplinary cybersecurity organization that includes governance, security architecture, offensive security, or comparable consulting disciplines.
Demonstrated financial accountability for a consulting or professional services organization, including revenue, margin, utilization, capacity, and project economics.
Experience managing project-based consulting delivered through fixed-fee, T&M, retainer, or comparable professional services models.
Ability to work effectively with Sales and pre-sales organizations without compromising the independence and risk-based approach of a vendor-neutral consulting practice.
Functional understanding of relevant regulations and industry standards (e.g., SOX, AICPA SOC Reporting Standards, ISO27001, PCI, NIST, HIPAA) and best practices and methodologies to address these requirements.
Experience developing workforce plans that balance permanent employees, demand, utilization, specialized skills, and external delivery capacity.
Experience managing subcontractors or third-party delivery resources while maintaining internal delivery capability as the primary foundation for growth.
Experience working directly with senior client executives and serving as an escalation point or executive sponsor for complex cybersecurity engagements.
Ability to manage consulting economics using revenue, gross profit, gross margin, utilization, backlog, capacity, forecasting, and project-level financial performance.
Strong understanding of cybersecurity consulting across GRC, security architecture, offensive security, application security, and cloud security.
Technical depth sufficient to challenge Principal Consultants on methodologies, technical approaches, service design, delivery quality, and emerging client requirements.
Ability to translate consulting demand and backlog into FTE hiring, development, subcontractor, and capacity decisions.
Demonstrated ability to improve utilization and margin without compromising delivery quality or creating unsustainable workloads.
Experience building repeatable consulting services, including methodology, scope, level-of-effort estimates, costing, staffing models, and delivery standards.
Ability to identify when consulting services should be expanded, redesigned, standardized, or retired based on performance and market demand.
Demonstrated success building collaborative teams across distinct technical disciplines and developing managers who can lead experienced practitioners.
Executive communication skills sufficient to advise and challenge senior client stakeholders and manage difficult delivery or commercial conversations.
Experience operating in a remote or geographically distributed delivery organization.
Ability to travel up to 30% for client engagements and internal meetings.

Experience developing technical enablement for Sales and pre-sales teams to improve identification and qualification of consulting opportunities.

jobs.title: Director, Cybersecurity GRC
jobs.description:
Job Description

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Director, Cybersecurity GRC manages the people, processes, and technology related to Momentive Software's Cybersecurity GRC group — overseeing governance, risk, and compliance activities including client audit support, RFP response, internal IT audit, and contract review. This role carries out GRC activities in alignment with the Firm's business objectives, regulatory requirements, and strategic goals, with a focus on recognized cybersecurity frameworks and contractual compliance.

The Director serves as the process owner for all IS GRC-related projects and activities and assists the CISO in planning, developing, and overseeing the cybersecurity program. The role integrates across Cybersecurity, Information Technology, new business development, the Office of General Counsel, and the professional responsibility function. In addition to ongoing governance and operational oversight, this position supports strategic alignment with the business, cybersecurity outreach, and expert guidance to internal and external stakeholders. As a strategic partner to the business, this role helps Momentive win and retain enterprise clients, support growth and M&A readiness, and position the GRC program as a business enabler — not just a compliance function.

Key Responsibilities

GRC Program Leadership

Maintain direct responsibility for all aspects of IS GRC, including governance, risk assessment, compliance, and audit support.
Ensure continual improvement of the cybersecurity program through effective application of technology, systems, processes, personnel development, and leadership.
Provide cybersecurity services that meet or exceed the Firm's professional, contractual, regulatory, and certification requirements.
Manage the Firm's IS GRC people, processes, and technology infrastructure, including creation and review of IS GRC standards, guidelines, and operating procedures.
Serve as the business owner for IS GRC toolsets, platforms, and processes.
Manage the IS GRC team budget.
Consult with Legal regarding acceptable contract terms and conditions related to cybersecurity.

ISMS & System Governance

Lead the System Governance Virtual Team, promoting continual ISMS improvement across the Firm.
Provide direction on risk assessment requirements and assistance evaluating risk treatment plans.
Provide input on the selection and design of IS controls.
Provide input on metrics developed to monitor and test the effectiveness of the Firm's IS controls.
Define documentation requirements to ensure compliance with ISMS requirements.
Advise the team on client contractual requirements and Firm commitments relative to GRC practices.
Assist the team in developing systems and processes that ensure ISMS compliance and continual improvement.
Maintain the Firm's Cybersecurity Management System (ISMS), including the creation and review of policies, standards, and procedures.
Enforce, monitor, and report on compliance with the Firm's ISMS.
Partner with the Director, AI Governance to co-develop and align AI policies, assess AI-related risks, and integrate AI governance practices into the ISMS framework.

Cybersecurity Operations & Engineering Integration

Work closely with Cybersecurity Operations and Engineering teams to define, develop, and facilitate efficient and effective service delivery.
Oversee integrated vendor and other risk assessment activities in coordination with technical teams.
Liaise with system and business owners to ensure new platforms comply with Firm cybersecurity requirements.
Serve within the Firm's Computer Cybersecurity Incident Response Team (CSIRT).

Compliance & Audit

Oversee cybersecurity risk assessments and provide audit mechanisms for the cybersecurity process.
Meet published SLAs for the provisioning and support of cybersecurity GRC operations and activities.
Provide evidence and expert support for client audits, RFP responses, and regulatory reviews.
Track compliance with applicable regulatory schemes and monitor changes in legislation and accreditation standards.

Cybersecurity Awareness & Culture

Manage the cybersecurity awareness program, including phishing simulation and constituent outreach initiatives.
Initiate, facilitate, and promote activities that foster cybersecurity awareness across the organization.
Maintain and contribute to the Firm's cybersecurity-related information repositories.

Leadership & People Management

Mentor and lead members of the Cybersecurity GRC group through effective performance reviews, development opportunities, and a culture of performance excellence.
Direct reports include TPRM Advisors, who manage third-party risk management activities across the organization; this role carries full people management accountability for that team.
Transform executive priorities into operational GRC initiatives with clear vision, support, and expectation-setting.
Provide status reports and relevant metrics to the CISO.
Serve in a proactive, consultative role to other business units and constituents.
Provide exemplary service to internal and external stakeholders, demonstrating empathy, respect, professionalism, and expertise.

Strategic Planning & Roadmap

Maintain situational and environmental awareness; implement appropriate tactics and strategies to protect the organization and support roadmap development.
Strike an appropriate balance between strategic leadership and operational contribution, using a hands-on approach to solving problems and meeting deliverables.
Participate in defining the Firm's DR/BCP practices as required.
Provide innovation within the cybersecurity realm.

Required

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

10-12+ years of experience in cybersecurity, with 3-5 years in a leadership or program management role.
Thorough knowledge of professional management practices including supervisory techniques, leadership principles, and employment practices.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including public speaking and the ability to convey complex cybersecurity concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
Ability to think and communicate strategically about the role of cybersecurity in a global organization.
Ability to quickly assess an organization's capability-maturity level and apply that knowledge to RFPs, audits, contract reviews, and internal operations.
Proficiency in at least one major EGRC/ITGRC platform (e.g., ServiceNow GRC, Archer, OneTrust, LogicGate).
Comprehensive understanding of major cybersecurity frameworks: NIST CSF, CIS Controls, SOC2T2, and COBIT.
Familiarity with common regulatory schemes including GDPR, PCI-DSS, GLBA, FISMA, HIPAA, and ITAR.
Advanced understanding of technical controls, how they address risk, and how they map to framework and regulatory requirements.
Broad understanding of TCP/IP, DNS, common network services, and foundational infrastructure concepts.
Knowledge of server, workstation, and Active Directory technologies as they relate to cybersecurity controls.
Familiarity with common cybersecurity monitoring technologies: SIEM, IDS, log management, and vulnerability assessment.
Ability to gather and analyze facts, define problems, draw conclusions, and recommend solutions.
Ability to maintain objectivity and composure under pressure.
Ability to set priorities independently given broad executive requirements.
Demonstrated flexibility in response to the ever-changing priorities of a service provider organization.
Rigorous and disciplined approach to operational oversight.

Preferred

One or more relevant certifications required or preferred: CISSP, CISM, or CRISC. ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor is a plus.

About Us

Momentive Software amplifies the impact of over 20,000 purpose-driven organizations in over 30 countries, with over $11 billion raised and 55 million members served to date. Mission-driven nonprofits and associations rely on Momentive’s cloud-based software and services to address their most pressing challenges – from engaging their communities to simplifying operations and growing revenue. Designed to help organizations connect more, manage more, and ultimately expect more, Momentive's solutions are built with reliability at the core and strategically focus on fundraising, learning, events, careers, volunteering, accounting, and association management. Momentive partners with organizations that believe "good enough" is never enough – so they can bring on better outcomes for everyone they serve. Learn more at momentivesoftware.com.

Why Work Here?

At Momentive Software, we’re a team of passionate problem-solvers, innovators, and volunteers who believe in using technology to make a real difference. We dream big, support each other, and take pride in creating solutions that help our customers drive meaningful change. If you’re looking for a place where your work matters and your ideas are valued, you’ll find it here.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Cybersecurity, CTEM & Vulnerability Intelligence - Remote
jobs.description:
Preference will be given to candidates residing in the Eastern or Central time zones.

As a Senior Manager, CTEM & Vulnerability Management, you will lead the enterprise Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM) and Vulnerability Management function across enterprise IT, cloud, operational technology (OT), and product environments. You will partner with Product Security, Threat Intelligence, Security Operations, Infrastructure, Cloud, and Engineering teams to reduce exposure through risk-based discovery, prioritization, validation, and remediation.

What you will do:

Technical Responsibilities:

Lead the enterprise CTEM and Vulnerability Management program, including its strategy, roadmap, and operating model.
Oversee vulnerability scanning and assessment across infrastructure, cloud, endpoint, application, identity, network, and OT environments.
Manage the product security vulnerability lifecycle with Product Security, including intake, triage, risk assessment, remediation tracking, software bill of materials (SBOM) analysis, and coordinated vulnerability disclosure support.
Prioritize vulnerabilities and exposures using CVSS, EPSS, CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV), threat intelligence, asset criticality, and business context.
Lead attack surface management, exposure validation, and breach and attack simulation activities to confirm exploitability and control effectiveness.
Evaluate emerging vulnerabilities, exploits, and threat intelligence affecting enterprise systems, marketed products, and embedded systems.
Drive automation for vulnerability discovery, data enrichment, ticketing, remediation workflows, and reporting through SOAR platforms, APIs, Python, or PowerShell.

Portage Point Partners is a business advisory, interim management and investment banking firm intensely focused on the middle market. Our blue chip team leverages bulge bracket experience in consulting, operations, finance, accounting, investment banking and investing to provide unmatched transactional, operational and financial perspectives to middle market stakeholders. The Portage Point cross-functional platform is uniquely architected to offer fully integrated capabilities and solutions that identify value capture, mitigate risk and positively impact outcomes at every stage of the ever-changing middle market business lifecycle. From ideation to monetization, Portage Point delivers excellence across transaction advisory services (TAS), transaction execution services (TES), office of the CFO (OCFO), performance improvement (PI), interim management (IM), investment banking (IB), operational turnaround and financial restructuring (TRS).

Recognized for accelerated growth, Portage Point Partners is consistently featured in rankings from Inc. 5000, The Financial Times and Consulting Magazine. This recognition is a testament to the firm’s focus on excellence, intensity and pace and ability to attract blue chip and bulge bracket talent committed to delivering impactful solutions.

The IB team advises founders, entrepreneurs, financial sponsors and investors across software, technology and tech services on M&A, debt and equity capital transactions, recapitalizations, and where applicable, restructurings,

363 sales, acquisition and Debtor-in-Possession (DIP) financings and liability management. Intensely focused on the middle market, our team delivers bespoke solutions and unique perspectives to every client. Our talent structure ensures clients receive top-level support throughout the entirety of the transaction and affords junior talent the opportunity to work directly alongside firm stakeholders.

The Vice President, Tech IB // M&A role offers an ideal opportunity for candidates with technology sector expertise to leverage the firm’s rapidly expanding platform to support the execution and delivery of all workflows necessary to consummate transactions for our middle-market clients. As a Vice President, Technology Investment Banking // M&A at Portage Point, you will work on a variety of transactions across software, technology and tech services that provide exposure to various investment banking services, including mergers and acquisitions, growth equity, private placements of debt and equity securities and other financial advisory services. The role represents a unique opportunity for a highly capable professional with a strong tech sector foundation to make substantial contributions to overall firm growth in a fast-paced and entrepreneurial environment.

Responsibilities

Work with the Portage Point Technology IB team (Associates to Managing Directors) to execute all deliverables necessary to consummate transactions for our middle-market technology clients primarily on domestic and cross-border M&A transactions
Play an integral role on Technology IB deal teams, provide execution support primarily for sell-side mergers and acquisitions, as well as occasional buy-side mandates, growth equity, private placements and other financial advisory services for clients
Lead the preparation of company valuations, financial models, company marketing documents and client presentations in addition to performing research and various analyses in support of new business generation
Create and present internal and external client deliverables
Support the creation of client marketing materials (Teasers, Confidential Information Presentations, Management Presentations, etc.) to be distributed to prospective investors
Aid with the management of, and compliance with, all administrative standard operating procedures associated with a transaction
Provide professional development coaching to junior team members
Share and manage best practices as well as lead internal trainings where required
Support business development efforts within the tech ecosystem, including origination and relationship-building with founders, financial sponsors and strategic acquirors, while maintaining strong relationships with existing clients
Maintain current knowledge of tech sector trends, financing activity and public and private market valuation benchmarks across various subsectors in software, tech and tech services
Support talent acquisition and firm development efforts
Contribute to creating a high-performing and inclusive culture

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree from a top undergraduate program
Located or willing to self-relocate to Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, New York or Philadelphia
Willing to go into the local Portage Point office four days a week
Willing to work at client sites as needed
Seven plus years of experience working for a top-tier investment bank at the Associate or Vice President level is preferred, with direct experience advising technology, software or tech services companies strongly preferred
Genuine interest in and knowledge of the tech sector including emerging trends across software, tech services and AI
Strong financial modeling skills and an excellent grasp of corporate finance and valuation methodologies including DCF, LBO, merger modeling, trading and transaction comparables, with fluency in tech-specific valuation frameworks (e.g. revenue and ARR based valuation, SaaS unit economics, retention metrics)
Series 79 and 63 licensing preferred or the ability to obtain within 120 days of employment
Ability to successfully work in a small, collaborative team environment
High degree of maturity with a proven ability to interact with senior executives, tech founders, private equity and growth equity firms, lenders, lawyers, middle managers and line workers
Effectively communicates analysis through Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook and PowerPoint including high-quality messaging, structure and formatting
Eagerness to be responsive at all times
Proven track-record of success in high pressure, time-constrained environments
Excellent written and verbal communication skills including strong e-mail etiquette
Top-tier organizational skills and attention to detail
Self-starter and entrepreneurial spirit

$400,000 - $600,000 a year

Job Description

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Director, Cybersecurity GRC manages the people, processes, and technology related to Momentive Software's Cybersecurity GRC group — overseeing governance, risk, and compliance activities including client audit support, RFP response, internal IT audit, and contract review. This role carries out GRC activities in alignment with the Firm's business objectives, regulatory requirements, and strategic goals, with a focus on recognized cybersecurity frameworks and contractual compliance.

The Director serves as the process owner for all IS GRC-related projects and activities and assists the CISO in planning, developing, and overseeing the cybersecurity program. The role integrates across Cybersecurity, Information Technology, new business development, the Office of General Counsel, and the professional responsibility function. In addition to ongoing governance and operational oversight, this position supports strategic alignment with the business, cybersecurity outreach, and expert guidance to internal and external stakeholders. As a strategic partner to the business, this role helps Momentive win and retain enterprise clients, support growth and M&A readiness, and position the GRC program as a business enabler — not just a compliance function.

Key Responsibilities

GRC Program Leadership

Maintain direct responsibility for all aspects of IS GRC, including governance, risk assessment, compliance, and audit support.
Ensure continual improvement of the cybersecurity program through effective application of technology, systems, processes, personnel development, and leadership.
Provide cybersecurity services that meet or exceed the Firm's professional, contractual, regulatory, and certification requirements.
Manage the Firm's IS GRC people, processes, and technology infrastructure, including creation and review of IS GRC standards, guidelines, and operating procedures.
Serve as the business owner for IS GRC toolsets, platforms, and processes.
Manage the IS GRC team budget.
Consult with Legal regarding acceptable contract terms and conditions related to cybersecurity.

ISMS & System Governance

Lead the System Governance Virtual Team, promoting continual ISMS improvement across the Firm.
Provide direction on risk assessment requirements and assistance evaluating risk treatment plans.
Provide input on the selection and design of IS controls.
Provide input on metrics developed to monitor and test the effectiveness of the Firm's IS controls.
Define documentation requirements to ensure compliance with ISMS requirements.
Advise the team on client contractual requirements and Firm commitments relative to GRC practices.
Assist the team in developing systems and processes that ensure ISMS compliance and continual improvement.
Maintain the Firm's Cybersecurity Management System (ISMS), including the creation and review of policies, standards, and procedures.
Enforce, monitor, and report on compliance with the Firm's ISMS.
Partner with the Director, AI Governance to co-develop and align AI policies, assess AI-related risks, and integrate AI governance practices into the ISMS framework.

Cybersecurity Operations & Engineering Integration

Work closely with Cybersecurity Operations and Engineering teams to define, develop, and facilitate efficient and effective service delivery.
Oversee integrated vendor and other risk assessment activities in coordination with technical teams.
Liaise with system and business owners to ensure new platforms comply with Firm cybersecurity requirements.
Serve within the Firm's Computer Cybersecurity Incident Response Team (CSIRT).

Compliance & Audit

Oversee cybersecurity risk assessments and provide audit mechanisms for the cybersecurity process.
Meet published SLAs for the provisioning and support of cybersecurity GRC operations and activities.
Provide evidence and expert support for client audits, RFP responses, and regulatory reviews.
Track compliance with applicable regulatory schemes and monitor changes in legislation and accreditation standards.

Cybersecurity Awareness & Culture

Manage the cybersecurity awareness program, including phishing simulation and constituent outreach initiatives.
Initiate, facilitate, and promote activities that foster cybersecurity awareness across the organization.
Maintain and contribute to the Firm's cybersecurity-related information repositories.

Leadership & People Management

Mentor and lead members of the Cybersecurity GRC group through effective performance reviews, development opportunities, and a culture of performance excellence.
Direct reports include TPRM Advisors, who manage third-party risk management activities across the organization; this role carries full people management accountability for that team.
Transform executive priorities into operational GRC initiatives with clear vision, support, and expectation-setting.
Provide status reports and relevant metrics to the CISO.
Serve in a proactive, consultative role to other business units and constituents.
Provide exemplary service to internal and external stakeholders, demonstrating empathy, respect, professionalism, and expertise.

Strategic Planning & Roadmap

Maintain situational and environmental awareness; implement appropriate tactics and strategies to protect the organization and support roadmap development.
Strike an appropriate balance between strategic leadership and operational contribution, using a hands-on approach to solving problems and meeting deliverables.
Participate in defining the Firm's DR/BCP practices as required.
Provide innovation within the cybersecurity realm.

Required

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

10-12+ years of experience in cybersecurity, with 3-5 years in a leadership or program management role.
Thorough knowledge of professional management practices including supervisory techniques, leadership principles, and employment practices.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including public speaking and the ability to convey complex cybersecurity concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
Ability to think and communicate strategically about the role of cybersecurity in a global organization.
Ability to quickly assess an organization's capability-maturity level and apply that knowledge to RFPs, audits, contract reviews, and internal operations.
Proficiency in at least one major EGRC/ITGRC platform (e.g., ServiceNow GRC, Archer, OneTrust, LogicGate).
Comprehensive understanding of major cybersecurity frameworks: NIST CSF, CIS Controls, SOC2T2, and COBIT.
Familiarity with common regulatory schemes including GDPR, PCI-DSS, GLBA, FISMA, HIPAA, and ITAR.
Advanced understanding of technical controls, how they address risk, and how they map to framework and regulatory requirements.
Broad understanding of TCP/IP, DNS, common network services, and foundational infrastructure concepts.
Knowledge of server, workstation, and Active Directory technologies as they relate to cybersecurity controls.
Familiarity with common cybersecurity monitoring technologies: SIEM, IDS, log management, and vulnerability assessment.
Ability to gather and analyze facts, define problems, draw conclusions, and recommend solutions.
Ability to maintain objectivity and composure under pressure.
Ability to set priorities independently given broad executive requirements.
Demonstrated flexibility in response to the ever-changing priorities of a service provider organization.
Rigorous and disciplined approach to operational oversight.

Preferred

One or more relevant certifications required or preferred: CISSP, CISM, or CRISC. ISO 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor is a plus.

About Us

Momentive Software amplifies the impact of over 20,000 purpose-driven organizations in over 30 countries, with over $11 billion raised and 55 million members served to date. Mission-driven nonprofits and associations rely on Momentive’s cloud-based software and services to address their most pressing challenges – from engaging their communities to simplifying operations and growing revenue. Designed to help organizations connect more, manage more, and ultimately expect more, Momentive's solutions are built with reliability at the core and strategically focus on fundraising, learning, events, careers, volunteering, accounting, and association management. Momentive partners with organizations that believe "good enough" is never enough – so they can bring on better outcomes for everyone they serve. Learn more at momentivesoftware.com.

Why Work Here?

At Momentive Software, we’re a team of passionate problem-solvers, innovators, and volunteers who believe in using technology to make a real difference. We dream big, support each other, and take pride in creating solutions that help our customers drive meaningful change. If you’re looking for a place where your work matters and your ideas are valued, you’ll find it here.

new_jobs.title: Director of Information Technology Consultant
new_jobs.description:
Director of Information Technology Consultant

Location: West Central Texas
Employment Type: Interim / Consulting Assignment
Duration: Approximately 3–6 months
Pay Rate: Approximately $125/hour, subject to final engagement structure
Work Arrangement: Onsite Monday–Thursday; approved temporary housing and travel expenses reimbursed

Position Overview

A public-sector organization in Texas is seeking an experienced Consultant - Director of Information Technology to provide executive leadership and operational continuity during a period of technology transformation.

This individual will lead enterprise technology operations while helping the organization strengthen service delivery, accountability, governance, cybersecurity, infrastructure, applications, and overall technology operations. The Interim Director will work closely with executive leadership, department leaders, technical teams, consultants, and service providers.

The ideal candidate is an experienced IT executive who can quickly assess an organization, establish priorities, stabilize operations, develop staff, manage risk, and advance an existing technology transformation roadmap while maintaining reliable day-to-day services.

Key Responsibilities

Provide executive leadership and accountability for enterprise IT operations and services.
Maintain continuity and reliability of critical technology services across a complex 24/7 operating environment.
Establish clear service ownership, accountability, performance expectations, escalation procedures, documentation, and backup coverage.
Assess organizational capabilities, staffing needs, service gaps, and operational priorities.
Coach and develop technology staff while utilizing vendors, consultants, and managed service providers as appropriate.
Strengthen IT service management practices across incidents, requests, problems, changes, service levels, knowledge management, assets, and continual improvement.
Partner with executive and departmental leadership to communicate technology risks, priorities, resource requirements, investments, and service performance.
Strengthen technology governance, project prioritization, architecture, cybersecurity, change management, and reporting processes.
Maintain and advance technology roadmaps and project portfolios while balancing operational demands, technical debt, cybersecurity, lifecycle requirements, and available resources.
Provide oversight across enterprise applications, data, integrations, automation, infrastructure, cloud platforms, networks, identity, endpoints, and workplace technology.
Support mission-critical and regulated technology environments, including public safety, emergency communications, operational technology, and other essential services.
Oversee cybersecurity, technology risk, incident response, resilience, recovery, and applicable compliance requirements.
Manage technology vendors, contracts, managed services, licensing, renewals, service levels, and deliverables.
Oversee technology budgets, investments, staffing requirements, and lifecycle planning.
Advance an established technology transformation roadmap and prepare the organization for a successful transition to permanent leadership.

Qualifications

Significant leadership experience within enterprise information technology.
Experience leading professional and technical teams, technology operations, budgets, vendors, and complex services.
Demonstrated success stabilizing technology operations and leading organizational or technology transformation.
Strong understanding of cybersecurity, resilience, infrastructure/cloud services, enterprise applications, data, service management, governance, enterprise architecture, and vendor management.
Experience supporting regulated, mission-critical, public safety, critical infrastructure, utility, government, or comparable 24/7 environments.
Experience with CJIS or comparable security and compliance environments is highly desirable.
Strong executive communication, decision-making, staff development, relationship management, financial management, and change leadership skills.
Bachelor's degree in a related discipline preferred; equivalent executive technology experience may be considered.
ITIL, PMP, CGCIO, CISSP, CISM, CRISC, COBIT, or similar certifications are desirable.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is a seasoned technology executive who is comfortable stepping into a complex organization, quickly establishing credibility, evaluating immediate priorities, and leading through change. Previous CIO, IT Director, Deputy CIO, Assistant IT Director, or comparable enterprise technology leadership experience within government, utilities, public safety, critical infrastructure, or another complex 24/7 environment would translate particularly well.

Please submit your resume in Word or PDF format to be considered.
